title: PragAlign: Evidence-Sensitive Reply Assistance Across Chinese and Japanese Appropriateness Judgments
abstract: arXiv:2608.26700v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Reply assistance in multilingual settings requires linguistic competence and culturally situated judgments of appropriateness. We present PragAlign, which separates context reading from selective clarification, and evaluate it alongside Direct and Rule. Nine native Chinese speakers judged Chinese materials, while three native Japanese speakers judged matched Japanese versions. In the Chinese evaluation, PragAlign received significantly better ranks than both baselines. In the Japanese evaluation, Direct had the lowest mean rank, PragAlign had the highest top-rank rate, and the omnibus difference was not significant. The groups selected the same top condition in 5 of 10 scenarios, including four shared PragAlign selections. The results identify shared and language-specific judgment patterns and inform reply assistance designed to support linguistic and cultural understanding.

translated_title: PragAlign：面向中日得体性判断的证据敏感回复辅助
translated_abstract: 多语言环境中的回复辅助需要语言能力和文化情境下的得体性判断。我们提出了PragAlign，它将上下文阅读与选择性澄清分离，并与Direct和Rule两种基线方法进行了评估。九名以中文为母语的评判者评估了中文材料，而三名以日语为母语的评判者评估了匹配的日文版本。在中文评估中，PragAlign获得的排名显著优于两种基线方法。在日文评估中，Direct的平均排名最低，PragAlign的最高排名率最高，但总体差异不显著。两组在10个场景中有5个选择了相同的顶级条件，其中包括四个共同的PragAlign选择。结果揭示了共性和语言特定的判断模式，并为旨在支持语言和文化理解的回复辅助提供了参考。
tldr: 本文提出PragAlign模型，通过分离上下文阅读与选择性澄清，在中日双语得体性判断中显著优于基线，揭示跨语言共性判断模式。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces PragAlign, which separates context reading from selective clarification, significantly outperforming baselines in Chinese and Japanese appropriateness judgments, revealing cross-linguistic shared patterns.
